item.title: Beyond the SDGs: What Did We Learn, and What Comes Next? — Tue Oct 20, 12:00 PM — Trent Drive Hall 040
item.description:
In 2015, United Nations member states adopted the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), a Blueprint for achieving a set of interconnected targets to advance global health, equity and development. With just four years left before the SDGs' 2030 end date, it's clear many of these milestones won't be met. What, then, was the value of adopting the SDGs, and what should come next?
With lessons from the SDGs as a guide, this Think Global panel will ask whether the world should adopt a new set of goals to succeed the SDGs after their 2030 expiration, and if so, what those goals should prioritize. Panelists will tackle these questions drawing on their diverse disciplines and expertise-political economy, public policy, family medicine, demography, disease modeling, financing and health economics.
Source: Duke University

item.title: Connect AI to Your Work — Tue Oct 20, 12:00 PM — None
item.description:
Ready to go beyond the basic chat? This session builds upon foundational AI and prompting skills to help you connect AI more deeply to the work you already do. Through practical examples, you'll learn how connected AI can help you organize projects, analyze data, find information, and support work across your productivity tools. We will explore plugins, skills, projects, and basic agents and learn how they can bring together your apps, information, and workflows to streamline everyday tasks. item.description:
What will life beyond Earth look and feel like for the first cosmic explorers?
Join the Duke SPACE Initiative for a networking lunch & seminar with analog astronaut and photographer, Cassandra Klos ('20).
An analog astronaut can be anyone -- an artist, a researcher, an engineer, an historian, or a scientist who plays the role of a space traveler during a simulated space mission on Earth.
They live and work in isolated habitats or extreme environments-such as deserts, the ocean floor, polar regions, caves, or specialized indoor facilities-that mimic the conditions of space, the Moon, or Mars.
Lunch begins at 11:30 AM. Talk begins at 12 PM.
This seminar is being organized by the Duke SPACE Initiative in collaboration with the Duke Center for Documentary Studies, Duke University's MFA|EDA program with support from Duke's Office of Interdisciplinary Programs.

item.description:
Learning in Networks Reading Group and Seminar Series: Tuesdays, 12pm in 330 Gross Hall; lunch included The institute focuses on fundamental questions in statistical inference, machine learning, causal inference, and optimization on networks, with particular emphasis on statistical-computational tradeoffs, message-passing algorithms, learning dynamics, and network-based market design. item.title: Women, Youth, and Anti-Colonial Struggle in South Africa’s Exiled Liberation Movements — Tue Oct 20, 12:00 PM — Smith Warehouse
item.description: Using the archives of the African National Congress of South Africa & the letters and memoirs of past activists, this talk will examine how women shaped the exiled struggle against apartheid in South Africa. From the 1960s through the 1980s, South African women pushed the mainstream of the anti-apartheid movement to consider women's particular suffering under apartheid, and to fight for broad social transformation as part of overthrowing apartheid. At the same time, within the movement, generational tensions also sparked conversation and at times heated disagreement over topics like sex education, access to birth control, and the right to family life within a militarized revolutionary movement. These challenging conversations reveal that younger generations of exiles brought new political ideas into the movement from the mid-1970s onwards, transforming an aging political organization into a more militant formation. item.title: Vintage Rides Ride — Sun Oct 25, 9:00 AM
item.description:
Carolina Tarwheels Cycling Club What is a Vintage Rides Ride? Well, it's where we pull out the old bikes and remember (or imagine) what it was like in the old days, when bikes were (mostly) steel, tires were skinny, jerseys were wool, and pedals had toe clips ("toe cages" to you younger folks). Shifters were generally on the down tube, and friction operated- no one had to charge any batteries before the ride. So bring your classics, or ride anything at all, but come along for a relaxed, easy ride. All riders and all bikes are welcome! Route here: [https://ridewithgps.com/routes/39713600](https://ridewithgps.com/routes/39713600) or something similar. **Route subject to change at the leader's whim** (often based on what kind of gearing we're on). item.title: The Story of Stone in the Culberson Asiatic Arboretum — Tue Nov 17, 10:00 AM — Duke Gardens–Barnes Welcome Center
item.description:
Join Paul Jones, founding curator of the Culberson Asiatic Arboretum, for a walking tour of some of the most iconic stone features found in the arboretum. You’ll hear the stories behind the stone, including traditional stone lanterns, pathways, waterfalls and lichen-covered boulders that blend seamlessly into the landscape. Hear why specific boulders were chosen and how they were placed, and learn more about the design intent. You’ll discover how a single carefully positioned rock can anchor an entire landscape, and how the interplay of stone, water and plants creates a sense of harmony that feels both timeless and deeply intentional. Fee: $22; free for Duke Gardens members with discount code. Parking: Parking fees apply.
Location: Meet at the Barnes Welcome Center.
Accessibility: This will be a small group program that takes place outdoors, traveling on a combination of paved and unpaved paths with some uneven surfaces and moderate inclines.
Source: Sarah P. Duke Gardens
